title: Microsoft Purview: apply default SharePoint library labels to existing files (GCC, GCC High, DoD)
summary: Hold: the PowerShell monitoring guidance says the progress command can check labeling failures, but Microsoft documents progress counts, not failure results, for that command. The roadmap facts, policy limits, licensing statements and listed control paths are otherwise supported; two checklist controls are missing from the table.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans automatic labeling of existing SharePoint files to match their library's default sensitivity label without relying on manual user labeling.
claims.quote: Enables auto-labeling of existing SharePoint files to match the default sensitivity label configured on their document library.

claims.claim: An administrator creates an auto-labeling policy and selects the option to apply library defaults to existing files.
claims.quote: When you create the policy, select the option to apply default sensitivity labels from SharePoint document libraries to existing files.

claims.claim: This policy type does not inspect file content to choose a label.
claims.quote: This policy type doesn't inspect file content to choose a label.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Eligible existing files receive the default sensitivity label selected for their library.
claims.quote: The label comes from the SharePoint document library's default sensitivity label setting.

claims.claim: Only one policy of this type can currently be created per tenant.
claims.quote: Currently, you can create one auto-labeling policy of this type per tenant

claims.where: What's changing; Scope; controls[0].note; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The policy can include up to 10 SharePoint sites.
claims.quote: include up to 10 SharePoint sites in the policy.

claims.claim: The policy evaluates only document libraries with a configured default sensitivity label.
claims.quote: The policy evaluates only SharePoint document libraries that have a default sensitivity label configured

claims.claim: The library default setting alone does not label existing files at rest.
claims.quote: Doesn't apply to existing files at rest in SharePoint.

claims.claim: The library default setting labels new files and files users edit, subject to existing-label precedence.
claims.quote: any new files uploaded to that library, or existing files edited in the library will have that label applied if they don't already have a sensitivity label

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The existing-files policy is admin-opt-in: an administrator creates it, runs simulation and turns it on before it labels files.
claims.quote: You can't automatically label documents and emails, or remove labels, until your policy has run at least one simulation.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Auto-applied sensitivity labels can apply encryption to SharePoint files.
claims.quote: When the auto-labeling policy includes locations for SharePoint or OneDrive, the label must be configured for the Assign permissions now setting, and User access to content expires must be set to Never.

claims.claim: Labels using user-defined permissions cannot be applied through this service-side policy.
claims.quote: When the auto-labeling policy includes locations for SharePoint or OneDrive, the label must be configured for the Assign permissions now setting

claims.claim: An encrypted label with user access expiry other than Never does not support a library default.
claims.quote: User access to content expires is set to a value other than Never.

claims.claim: Double Key Encryption labels do not support a library default.
claims.quote: some label configurations that apply encryption aren't suitable for SharePoint, and so don't support a default sensitivity label for a SharePoint document library: ... Double Key Encryption is selected.

claims.claim: General apply-label auto-labeling policies preserve manually applied labels by default.
claims.quote: Default behavior whether automatic labeling will override an existing label: ... When content has been manually labeled, that label won't be replaced by automatic labeling.

claims.claim: Automatic labeling replaces a lower-priority automatically applied label.
claims.quote: Automatic labeling will replace a lower priority sensitivity label that was automatically applied, but not a higher priority label.

claims.claim: Learn does not explicitly say whether the manual-label override setting is offered in the library-default policy wizard.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint library default existing files auto-labeling policy GCC cloud availability manual label override Additional label settings; read the auto-labeling page's override, library-default and wizard sections. General override is documented, but this wizard's settings can vary.

claims.claim: Creating this policy requires permissions to create and manage auto-labeling policies.
claims.quote: You have permissions to create and manage auto-labeling policies.

claims.claim: Creating the policy also requires metadata-read access, for which Learn names Compliance Administrator or an existing role such as SharePoint Administrator.
claims.quote: For the currently supported configuration path, use Compliance Administrator or an existing SharePoint or Microsoft Entra role with this access, such as SharePoint Administrator.

claims.claim: Turning a policy on requires Compliance Administrator or Compliance Data Administrator.
claims.quote: Turning a policy from Ready to turn on to On requires Compliance Administrator or Compliance Data Administrator.

claims.claim: A SharePoint site admin sets or changes each library's default sensitivity label.
claims.quote: This configuration is done by a SharePoint site admin: Add a sensitivity label to SharePoint document library.

claims.claim: The policy labels existing files service-side without requiring users to open them.
claims.quote: You want service-side labeling for files at rest, instead of relying on users to open or edit each file.

claims.claim: The general auto-labeling wizard offers automatic activation if the policy is not edited for 7 days.
claims.quote: Then decide whether to automatically turn on the policy if it's not edited for 7 days

claims.claim: Open, checked-out, locked, unsupported or unsupported-encrypted files might not be labeled.
claims.quote: Files might not be labeled if they're open, checked out, locked, unsupported, encrypted in an unsupported way, or otherwise unavailable when the policy evaluates them.

claims.claim: The This file has been automatically labeled tooltip also appears for auto-labeling policies and user default labels from label policies.
claims.quote: It also displays when sensitivity labels are applied by using auto-labeling policies or as a result of a user's default label from sensitivity label policies.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Learn documents replacing the policy's site selection with the next batch after labeling completes and results are reviewed.
claims.quote: After labeling for those sites is complete and you've reviewed the results, edit the policy to replace the site selection with the next batch of up to 10 sites.

claims.claim: E3 or Business Premium manual labeling entitlement does not include automatic labeling.
claims.quote: You have E3 or Business Premium. Manual labeling entitlement doesn't include automatic labeling.

claims.claim: Administrators configuring these features need the applicable licenses.
claims.quote: Administrators configuring these features need the applicable licenses.

claims.claim: Owners and members of shared locations such as SharePoint sites need the required licenses when the feature is used there.
claims.quote: Users with owner or member roles need the required licenses when the feature is used there.

claims.claim: Visitors and view-only users do not need a license for that benefit.

claims.claim: The licensing model for these Microsoft 365 Information Protection assets is per-user.
claims.quote: This licensing model enables you to apply Microsoft Purview controls and protections to Microsoft 365 and Windows/macOS endpoint-based assets.
claims.fix: Keep per-user and add https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/purview-billing-models to sources; its Per-user licensing model section explicitly identifies the Microsoft 365 E3/E5/A5/F5/G5 model.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: No separate licensing entry is published specifically for the existing-files library-default policy type.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint library default existing files auto-labeling policy pricing meter licensing; read the policy section and Purview service description sensitivity-labeling tables. They name service-side automatic labeling and library defaults, not a separate existing-files policy entry.

claims.claim: Learn documents no meter for this existing-files library-default policy.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint library default existing files auto-labeling policy pricing meter licensing; opened the policy page, service description and Purview billing models. The billing tables do not list this policy as a metered capability.

claims.claim: Sensitivity labels must be enabled for Office files in SharePoint and OneDrive.
claims.quote: Sensitivity labels are enabled for Office files in SharePoint and OneDrive.

claims.claim: Sensitivity labels usable as library defaults must be created and published.
claims.quote: The sensitivity labels that can be used as default library labels are created and published to the appropriate users or groups.

claims.claim: Selected sites need at least one library with a default sensitivity label.
claims.quote: In portal experiences that validate default library labels, each selected SharePoint site needs at least one library with a default sensitivity label.

claims.claim: Library defaults require labels scoped to Files & other data assets.
claims.quote: sensitivity labels that include the label scope of Files & other data assets

claims.claim: Library defaults are unavailable on libraries with SharePoint IRM enabled.
claims.quote: If a library is enabled for IRM, you won't be able to select a default sensitivity label.

claims.claim: This policy requires specific SharePoint sites rather than All.
claims.quote: Select specific SharePoint sites rather than All.

claims.claim: This policy type does not support administrative-unit scoping.
claims.quote: This policy type doesn't support administrative-unit scoping, so the simplified wizard doesn't include the Assign admin units step.

claims.claim: (Get-SPOTenant).EnableAIPIntegration checks whether sensitivity labels are enabled for Office files.
claims.quote: To check this status, you can run (Get-SPOTenant).EnableAIPIntegration from the SharePoint Online Management Shell to confirm the value is set to True.

claims.claim: Policy creation is reached in Microsoft Purview portal through Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies > + Create auto-labeling policy.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies. ... Select + Create auto-labeling policy.

claims.claim: No automation parameter for creating this library-default policy type is documented in New-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy.
claims.quote: Searched: New-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy library default labels existing files policy parameter; read its syntax and searched its full reference for library, default and PolicyTemplateInfo. No documented parameter or template value identifies this policy type.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies > policy > Turn on policy activates the policy after simulation.
claims.quote: Select your policy to see the details of the configuration and status ... When you're ready to run the policy without simulation, select the Turn on policy option.

claims.claim: Set-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy -Identity <AutoLabelingPolicyName> -Mode Enable turns an existing auto-labeling policy on.
claims.quote: The Identity parameter specifies the auto-labeling policy that you want to modify. ... Enable: The policy is enabled for actions and notifications.

claims.claim: TestWithoutNotifications is the test or simulation mode without actions or notifications.
claims.quote: TestWithoutNotifications: An audit mode where no actions are taken, and no notifications are sent (Test mode).

claims.claim: No admin UI is documented for the tenant-wide library-default labeling switch.
claims.quote: Searched: DisableDocumentLibraryDefaultLabeling tenant UI portal switch existing files policy ActionScourceDetails library default labels; opened the library-default page and read the Set-SPOTenant search excerpt. The documented tenant switch requires PowerShell.

claims.claim: Set-SPOTenant -DisableDocumentLibraryDefaultLabeling $true turns off library default labeling at tenant level.
claims.quote: This is a tenant-level setting that requires you to use the Set-SPOTenant cmdlet with the DisableDocumentLibraryDefaultLabeling parameter set to True

claims.claim: The tenant switch takes about 15 minutes to take effect.
claims.quote: it takes about 15 minutes for the change to take effect.

claims.claim: The tenant switch removes the option to configure library defaults for new or existing libraries.
claims.quote: You won't be able to select a default sensitivity label for new or existing libraries.

claims.claim: The switch deactivates existing library default selections so new files no longer receive them.
claims.quote: The label selection for the document library remains but is deactivated so new files won't have the selected sensitivity label applied.

claims.claim: Turning off library default labeling does not remove labels already applied as defaults.
claims.quote: Sensitivity labels that were applied as a default label aren't removed.

claims.claim: Learn does not say whether DisableDocumentLibraryDefaultLabeling stops the existing-files auto-labeling policy.
claims.quote: Searched: DisableDocumentLibraryDefaultLabeling tenant UI portal switch existing files policy ActionScourceDetails library default labels; read How to turn off this feature and the existing-files policy section. The switch's documented effects concern library selection and new files.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies > policy > View details opens policy labeling review pages.
claims.quote: go to Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies. Select a policy, then select View details in the policy details panel.

claims.claim: Get-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy -Identity "<policy name>" -IncludeProgressFeedback retrieves labeling progress for the selected policy.
claims.quote: If you use this switch, the command shows the progress of files to be labeled, files labeled in the last 7 days, and total files labeled for enabled auto-labeling policies.

claims.claim: Get-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy with -IncludeProgressFeedback can check labeling failures as an alternative to View details.
claims.quote: Searched: Get-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy IncludeProgressFeedback labeling failures failed files; read the full Get reference and policy monitoring section. The command documents pending and labeled counts; failure results are documented in the portal's Labeling failures view.
claims.fix: Replace the After rollout bullet with: 'Open View details for the policy to check labelled items and failures; use Get-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy with -IncludeProgressFeedback to check labelling progress counts.' Add to controls[3].note: 'The PowerShell call reports progress counts; investigate failures in the portal.' Keep the call unchanged. References: https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/exchangepowershell/get-autosensitivitylabelpolicy and https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/apply-sensitivity-label-automatically.

claims.quote: Searched: ActionScourceDetails default library existing files auto-labeling policy audit value; read library-default monitoring and searched the full auto-labeling page for ActionScourceDetails. Value 6 is documented for library defaults, not separately for this policy type.

claims.claim: Simulation results for this policy identify expected sites, libraries, default labels and files for review before activation.
